title: Bounded rationality
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, e-rational, teaches the rational maximising model and only mentions in passing that real people do not always fit it, so it does not teach bounded rationality and its settle-for-good-enough idea.

draft.title: Bounded rationality
card: Bounded rationality is the idea that people cannot make perfectly rational decisions. Their rationality has limits.
The limits are time, information and brain power. People rarely have the time to compare every option, all the facts, or the ability to process them.
So people often settle for a choice that is good enough, rather than searching for the best one. They may use rules of thumb, such as buying a familiar brand.
This differs from the traditional assumption that people collect all information and pick the option that gives the most satisfaction.
draft.remember: Limited time, information and brain power lead people to settle for good enough.

a.q: Why do people often make good enough decisions rather than the best ones?
opts: They face limits on time, information and brain power
They prefer to spend now rather than save for later
They care more about fairness than about their own gain
They are shown a high price before the real price
a.why: Bounded rationality is about the limits on how well people can compare options. The other options describe different ideas: willpower, self-interest and anchoring.
a.clue: Think about what stops someone comparing every option.

b.q: Priya needs a phone plan today. She checks three plans from one shop, picks one that suits her and does not search further. What does this show?
opts: She settled for a good enough choice with limited time
She chose the best plan out of all those available
She ignored her own interests to be fair to others
She gave in to what felt good now over later benefits
b.why: Priya has little time and did not compare every plan, so she took a choice that works. That is bounded rationality. She cannot know it was the best plan out of all available.
b.clue: Did Priya compare every plan on the market?

a.best: They face limits on time, information and brain power

b.best: She settled for a good enough choice with limited time
